introduction: The function of ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) is dependent on protein– protein and protein–RNA interactions.
Chemical crosslinking with mass spectrometry [XL-MS;, top right] is used for mapping protein–protein interactions.
On the other hand, the detection of RNA-linked peptides by mass spectrometry (MS) is challenging, given complex MS signals of low intensity.

This challenge is met by the RBDmap method: allow- ing to detect protein–RNA interactions using UV crosslinking fol- lowed by tandem proteolysis, using LysC or ArgC followed by trypsin, combined with MS (, 2017; ) (, top left).
Software packages are available for initial processing of XL-MS data
[e.g. pLink ] or RBDmap data
However, in an RBDmap experiment, the MS-identified peptides are adjacent to the RNA-linked peptides (, 2017).
Therefore, downstream bioinformatic analysis reveals the RNA-linked pepti- des, given the protein sequence and the proteases used in the assay.
Hence, custom pipelines are needed to combine, compare or reduce datasets obtained from different experiments, treatments and repli- cates, especially if RBDmap is complemented by XL-MS.
Such cus- tom analysis has remained a bottleneck for the study of RNP complexes when both protein–protein and protein–RNA interac- tions are of interest.

Herein, we describe crisscrosslinkeR, an R package aimed to identify molecular interactions detected from both types of XL-MS experiments—XL-MS and RBDmap—and to map both protein– protein and protein–RNA interactions, respectively.

criss crosslinkeR can map these different types of molecular interactions to the sequence or the three-dimensional (3D) structure of the same macromolecule complex(es), while comparing multiple experiments or treatments and accounting for experimental repli- cates [see Supplementary Material S1 for an example and Supplementary Table S1 for a comparison with other tools (,, and ) (, V C

crisscrosslinkeR was designed to fill the gap between the primary analysis of MS data to the interpret- ation and visualization of the results either simultaneously for both protein–RNA interactions and protein–protein interactions, or in- dependently for any of them.
To our knowledge, it is the first tool that streamlines RBDmap data analysis and the first package dedi- cated for mapping both RBDmap and XL-MS data.
Implementation Primary MS data analysis is performed by pLink, MaxQuant and Andromeda, which identify tryptic peptides from raw MS files (.raw) (, middle).

In the context of the MS data analysis pipeline, crisscrosslinkeR is placed downstream of these software and utilizes R packages and APIs for protein data bank (PDB) file reading and the RCSB PDB mapping.

Features Data reduction is done across multiple samples, allowing to merge replicates or accept data points based on user-defined conditions (e.g. only if the same crosslinked peptide appeared in n replicates).
Filtration is based on significance scores that were assigned during the primary data analysis.
crisscrosslinkeR is designed to handle an unlimited number of XL-MS and RBDmap datasets simultaneously for a direct comparison or data reduction, based on user preference.

There are currently no tools to visualize RBDmap data over sequences [two-dimensional (2D) visualization] or structures (3D visualization) of protein complexes, though these forms of visualiza- tion are popular and supported in case of XL-MS.
crisscrosslinkeR illustrate replicates or different experimental treatments for 2D rep- resentation of RBDmap data.
For 2D visualization of XL-MS and, optionally, RBDmap data, crisscrosslinkeR exports files compatible with the user-friendly server xiView (, bottom right).

For 3D visualization of RBDmap and XL-MS data, crisscrosslinkeR uses the RCSB PDB mapping API to identify the most suitable 3D structure(s) in the PDB, aligns it to the sequence of the protein used during the experiment and then uses the selected structure for 3D visualization of either RBDmap or XL-MS data (, bottom left).
Specifically, crisscrosslinkeR generates a Python script to launch PyMOL —a popular and stable suite for molecular imaging—to generate publication- quality figures or for structural analysis.

crisscrosslinkeR can be used to hide or present color-coded crosslinking sites, including based on the score applied by the primary software that detected them [MaxQuant or pLink ], the number of times linked peptides was detected across multiple replicates and differential crosslinked sites and, when ap- plicable, the Euclidean crosslinking distances; all these are visualized with large flexibility for user-defined color selection.
Collectively, crisscrosslinkeR is a versatile pipeline that stream- lines the workflow, starting from multiple raw data files down to publication-quality figures.
discussion: crisscrosslinkeR provides users with the ability to analyze and visual- ize data obtained from both RBDmap and XL-MS experiments including an unlimited number of replicates and treatments.

crisscrosslinkeR allows the user to combine replicates, or to search for common crosslinking events among replicates or different treat- ments, in order to discover biological cues in a complex dataset.
These functionalities are complemented by 2D and 3D visualization, tailored for subsequent communication of the results.
The current version of crisscrosslinker does not support solvent-accessible distan- ces.
These can be obtained using other software packages as Xwalk Jwalk and DynamXL.

To our knowledge, crisscrosslinkeR is the first available package that streamlines XL-MS data analysis for the discovery of both protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions within the same macromolecular RNP complex or biological system.
